text: I charge you before God and Christ Jesus, who is to judge the living and the dead, and by his appearing and his kingdom:
preach the word; be ready whether the time is right or not; correct, rebuke, and encourage—with all patience and careful teaching.
For the time is coming when people will not put up with sound teaching. Instead, to suit their own desires, they will gather around themselves a crowd of teachers to tickle their ears,
and they will turn their ears away from the truth and wander off after myths.
But you—keep a clear head in everything, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, carry out your ministry to the full.
As for me, I am already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time of my departure has come.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
From now on there is reserved for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will award to me on that day—and not only to me, but to all who have loved his appearing.

versions.text: From now on there is reserved for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will award me on that day—and not only to me, but to all who have longed for his appearing.
versions.explanation: The clause shifts from "award me" to "not only to me," creating a small grammatical mismatch when read aloud. Using "award to me" keeps the parallel prepositional phrasing consistent.

versions.text: From now on there is reserved for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will award to me on that day—and not only to me, but to all who have longed for his appearing.
versions.explanation: The Greek verb is ἀγαπάω (perfect participle, "have loved"), not a verb of longing. "Longed for" is a widely used dynamic rendering and reads smoothly, but "have loved his appearing" preserves the verb's actual sense and the perfect aspect while remaining just as speakable.

text: Do your best to come to me soon.
For Demas, in love with this present age, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica; Crescens has gone to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.

versions.text: Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me in the ministry.
versions.explanation: εἰς διακονίαν has no article in Greek and refers to practical service/help rather than a defined office; "for service" is closer to the sense and reads cleanly aloud.

text: Tychicus I have sent to Ephesus.
When you come, bring the cloak I left with Carpus at Troas, and the scrolls—especially the parchments.
Alexander the metalworker did me a great deal of harm; the Lord will repay him according to his deeds.
Be on your guard against him too, for he strongly opposed our message.
At my first defense no one stood by me; everyone abandoned me. May it not be held against them.
But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so that through me the message might be fully proclaimed and all the nations might hear it. And I was rescued from the lion's mouth.
The Lord will rescue me from every evil work and bring me safely into his heavenly kingdom. To him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.
Erastus stayed in Corinth, and I left Trophimus ill at Miletus.
Do your best to come before winter. Eubulus sends you greetings, and so do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers and sisters.
The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.
